title: Majestic Corner
reviewNotes: Four branches and 15 checked positions. Root after illustrated ...Rh2 reconstructed from stable Rf7 diagram and preceding move; transient opening pawn drag resolved as h7. Separate ...Rd8 node rotates the checking fork. Corrected source passive-defense example: Rf7 draws but ...Kd2 loses to Rf2+; supplied independent ...Rh3 drawing defense and explicit winning completion.

So, let's see what happens. If black plays rook to h2, if white tries to defend the pawn, now there is no progress to be made. Black is simply going to threaten a checkmate in one move. White has to move away and then black can still continue to create this threat and white can never promote. But as it turns out, white does have a pretty simple but incredible idea that allows [music] to promote the pawn by force. We start with rook to f1 check. So, the move is rook to f2, a beautiful sacrifice forking the king and [music] the rook. Well, okay, but black had another way of stopping this pawn, [music] right? If we go back to the start of the game, the rook could have gone to d8 and stopped the promotion like this. But the beautiful thing about a symmetrical board like the one that we use [music] in chess is that some ideas just happen to work on any side of this board. This is a check.
